chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asamm from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Ma'mar ibn Yahya that he heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will not call a servant to account for a prayer after the obligatory prayer, nor for charity after the obligatory alms-tax, nor for fasting after the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: What voluntary acts of worship will Allah not question a servant about according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that Allah does not hold servants accountable for neglecting voluntary (nafl) acts of worship, as the obligatory pillars (fard) suffice for the completion of duty. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that while voluntary acts are meritorious, their omission does not incur punishment, distinguishing them from the strict accountability of fard acts. The narration emphasizes the sufficiency of the core obligations, offering reassurance to believers regarding the completeness of their worship.
